title: The 8 AM Regret 101 group chat just got a photo of tomorrow's exam key. 140 people saw it.

outcomes.text: You mute the chat and study at the library until security turns the lights off at you. Twice.
You peek and memorize. The exam matches. You feel smart for exactly as long as it takes to remember why.
Dr. Pruitt wrote a fake key and leaked it himself. Question one: 'Who shared this?' You studied the wrong answers.
Dr. Pruitt wakes up long enough to write a brand-new exam. The chat is furious and has a theory about who told.

later.text: Remember telling Dr. Pruitt about the leaked key? He gave you five points of extra credit 'for being awake.' Highest compliment he has.

title: In the dining hall, an upperclassman leans in: 'Heard you're flexible. Last year's Clout Theory final, C$80.'

options.label: Pass
options.get: A clean grade, maybe a worse one

outcomes.text: 'Nah.' He shrugs and moves to the next table. You study Clout Theory, which is mostly about why he exists.

options.label: Buy it
options.cost: C$80 and a little more of your name

outcomes.text: Half the questions are the same. You pass, rested and C$80 poorer.
Prof. Tanabe rewrote the whole final. You bought a souvenir. A C$80 souvenir.

options.label: Buy it and share it
options.get: A study group that owes you
options.cost: C$80, and a lot of witnesses
options.riskWhy: Ten people can't keep a secret

outcomes.text: You send it to your study group. Instant legend. Eleven people, one old exam, zero discretion.

later.text: Remember sharing last year's Clout Theory final? Prof. Tanabe found it in the group chat. Everyone in it retakes, and they know who sent it.

title: Group Project Survival: your three teammates haven't opened the slides. It's due at 9 AM.

outcomes.text: You make 22 slides by 4 AM. Four names on the title slide. Dr. Osei says, 'One person did this.' He's looking at you.

options.label: Do it, leave their names off

outcomes.text: One name on the slide: yours. It's accurate. It's also a declaration of war.

later.text: Remember leaving your teammates off the slides? They posted a long thread called 'erased.' It does not mention that they did nothing.

outcomes.text: Dr. Osei sighs. He's heard this every semester since 2009. He splits the grade by who did what.

later.text: Remember telling Dr. Osei about your group? He put you with the three keenest people in class for the next project. They're terrifying. You aced it.

title: At Grand Street CC, the professor loves your group's best slide. Tomás made it. He's out sick.

outcomes.text: 'Tomás made that one.' The professor writes it down. Tomás, on the video call from bed, gives a feverish thumbs-up.
'Team effort.' The professor nods. Nobody's lying exactly. Nobody's telling the truth exactly either.
'That one was mine.' The professor beams and asks you to present it at the department fair.

later.text: Remember claiming Tomás's slide at Grand Street CC? He watched the recording. He's back, and he told the class exactly how he made it.

title: A flyer by the campus library: 'Guaranteed A. Any essay. C$90. Also wedding toasts.'

outcomes.text: You write it yourself, mostly at 2 AM. Prof. Vale writes 'Main character energy!' in the margin. You frame it.

options.label: Buy one
options.riskWhy: They sell the same essay to many

outcomes.text: The essay arrives in an hour. It's good. It's suspiciously good. It mentions a wedding.

later.text: Remember the C$90 essay from the flyer? It was also sold to eleven classmates. Prof. Vale noticed. Rewrite, and 'a conversation.'

options.label: Buy one, rewrite it all
options.cost: C$90 and still a night's work

outcomes.text: You buy it, then rewrite every sentence in your own words. It's basically yours now, and you paid C$90 for an outline.

title: A student on the St. Johnsons quad offers you C$120 to write his 'Main Character Energy' essay by Friday.

outcomes.text: 'Write it yourself, main character.' He looks hurt, then inspired, then hurt again.

options.label: Offer to tutor him, C$60
options.riskWhy: He may not want to learn

outcomes.text: Two hours at the library. He writes it himself. It's bad, but it's his. He pays C$60 and says it 'felt weird, in a good way.'

options.label: Write it for C$120
options.cost: A night, and a bit of integrity

outcomes.text: You write him a great essay. Too great: it's clearly not his voice. He pays and says 'perfect, bro.'

later.text: Remember the essay you wrote on the St. Johnsons quad? He got a B-minus and wants half back. And he told his whole floor you're 'available.'

title: Your work-study job at the campus library: shelve for one hour, log three. The supervisor naps from 2 to 4.

outcomes.text: You log one hour, then spend two more studying in the stacks for free. The supervisor snores approvingly.

options.label: Log all three
options.riskWhy: The book scanner logs every shelf

outcomes.text: Three hours logged, one worked. You nap in the reference section. Everybody here is napping.

later.text: Remember logging three hours for one at the campus library? The book scanner logged 11 books. Your supervisor woke up for this one.

outcomes.text: You shelve every book in the building, including some that were already shelved. C$45, earned.
